title: What if the next AI breakthrough isn’t a better chatbot?
summary: GPT learns through language, but JEPA learns from the world. What does this mean for next-gen API?
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority Love it or hate it, AI is increasingly good at helping write your emails, summarise a 100-page report, explain quantum physics, and generate a convincing image of just about anything. Give a modern AI model the right tools , and it can tackle complex, multi-step tasks, write code, and even build a small app or game with surprisingly little input. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini , and their competitors showcase increasingly impressive reasoning and agentic capabilities. But you’ve probably noticed some limitations, too. Sycophantic responses, overly verbose or formulaic prose, and difficulty grappling with the subtleties of complex problems remain familiar frustrations. It’s far from perfect. body: TL;DR Google is bringing Gemini to Google Sheets on iPhones, following its rollout on the web and Android. The feature is rolling out to eligible Google Workspace and Google AI subscribers and could take up to 15 days to reach everyone. Working with spreadsheets on a phone can be a pain, especially with hundreds of rows and columns. Google wants to make that experience less frustrating, and it’s now bringing Gemini to Google Sheets on iPhones. It is already available in Google Sheets on the web and, more recently, on Android . With its arrival on iOS , you can now ask Gemini questions about your spreadsheets, get quick summaries, and even create charts without pulling out your laptop. For example, say you’re looking at a spreadsheet tracking your monthly expenses. Instead of reviewing every transaction yourself, you can ask Gemini where you’ve spent the most. An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan Explanation: This is an unusual rainbow. For one thing, the rainbow is not complete, appearing only in a sunlit fan — but that by itself is not very unusual. What is most unusual is the fake location of the Sun . The Sun appears to be toward the front, just below those hills — but it is not. That is not how rainbows work . Rainbows involve a backward reflection from falling rain , so that the Sun must really be behind you . In this case, gaps between clouds near the setting Sun allowed rays to cross the entire sky and appear to converge in front , an unusual phenomenon called anticrepuscular rays . The photo was taken with a phone last week at sunset in Presenzano , Italy . The seemingly reverse rainbow was noticed when hanging up laundry . title: I’ve been a smart home user for 10 years, and the Apple HomeView looks like a game-changer

body: Smart displays are a category that, to me, have always felt like they’re on the cusp of being the next big thing for the smart home. I was excited when I first got my Nest Hub . title: I’ve been using an AI agent for a month, and I’m both impressed and terrified
summary: Instinct AI is extremely good, with some big caveats.
body: We’ve reached a pretty interesting point with AI. For the longest time, I’ve mostly used AI tools to ask questions or to write emails and summarize long PDFs. But AI agents are starting to change that. If you’re unfamiliar with the difference between an AI chatbot and an AI agent, it’s pretty simple. While a chatbot mostly gives you answers or helps you figure out how to do something, an AI agent can actually perform those tasks for you. For example, instead of asking AI to draft an email, you can ask an agent to find the relevant information, write the email, and send it on your behalf.
